title: What time is it?
goal: Tell the time, name the days, and make appointments — and learn the habit that trips up many learners: Pashto counts the half hour FORWARD, like English "half past seven", not backward like German "halb acht".
bekal: ask and tell the time, including half and quarter hours
name the seven days of the week and five parts of the day
make appointments and agree on a time to meet

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — وعده
dialogs.intro: Late afternoon. Najib has to work tomorrow, so they agree on when to meet and where to go.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.id: Budi, what time do you get up tomorrow?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه تل شپږ بجې پاڅېږم. ولې؟
lines.baca: zə təl shpaẓ baje pātsīẓəm. wale?
lines.id: I always get up at six. Why?
lines.literal: I always six o'clock get-up-I. why?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: زه اته بجې کار ته ځم. مونږ اووه نیمې بجې ډوډۍ خورو.
lines.baca: zə atə baje kār ta dzəm. mūẓ owə nīme baje ḍoḍəy khorū.
lines.id: I leave for work at eight. We'll have breakfast at half past seven.
lines.literal: I eight o'clock work to go-I. we seven half o'clock food eat-we.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: اووه نیمې بجې؟ دا اووه پنځه دېرش دی؟
lines.baca: owə nīme baje? dā owə pindzə-dersh day?
lines.id: Seven and a half? Does that mean 7:35?
lines.literal: seven half o'clock? this seven five-thirty is?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نه، اووه دېرش. نیمه تل مخکې ساعت ته اضافه کېږي.
lines.baca: nə, owə dersh. nīma təl məkhke sā'at ta izāfa keẓī.
lines.id: No, 7:30. The half is always added to the hour that has passed.
lines.literal: no, seven thirty. half always front hour to added becomes.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: آه، دا زمونږ برعکس دی. مونږ وایو نیمه اته.
lines.baca: āh, dā zmūẓ bar'aks day. mūẓ wāyū nīma atə.
lines.id: Ah, that's the opposite of ours. In Indonesian we say "half eight".
lines.literal: ah, this of-us opposite is. we say-we half eight.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.id: Yes, foreigners always get lost here.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ښه، اوس پوهېږم. تاسو کله بېرته راځئ؟
lines.baca: ṣa, os poheẓəm. tāso kəla berta rādzəy?
lines.id: OK, now I understand. When do you get back?
lines.literal: good, now understand-I. you(pl) when back come-you(pl)?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: ماسپښین څلور بجې. بیا پارک ته ځو.
lines.baca: māspaṣīn tsalor baje. byā pārk ta dzū.
lines.id: At four in the afternoon. Then we'll go to the park.
lines.literal: afternoon four o'clock. then park to go-we.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: او جمعه؟ جمعه هم کار کوئ؟
lines.baca: aw juma? juma ham kār kawəy?
lines.id: And Friday? Do you work on Friday too?
lines.literal: and Friday? Friday also work do-you(pl)?

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: نه، جمعه رخصتي ده. هره جمعه کورنۍ راټولېږي.
lines.baca: nə, juma rukhsatī da. hara juma kornəy rāṭoleẓī.
lines.id: No, Friday is the day off. Every Friday the family gets together.
lines.literal: no, Friday holiday is. every Friday family gathers.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: په اندونیزیا کې یکشنبه رخصتي وي.
lines.baca: pə Indonezyā ke yakshanbe rukhsatī wī.
lines.id: In Indonesia, Sunday is the day off.
lines.literal: in Indonesia in Sunday holiday usually-is.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: زمونږ اونۍ له شنبې څخه پیل کېږي.
lines.baca: zmūẓ onəy lə shanbe tsəkha pīl keẓī.
lines.literal: of-us week from Saturday-from from start becomes.

lines.speaker: نجیب:
lines.text: سبا سه شنبه ده. اووه نیمې بجې! هېر یې نه کړئ.
lines.baca: sabā se-shanbe da. owə nīme baje! her ye nə kṛəy.
lines.id: Tomorrow is Tuesday. Half past seven! Don't forget.
lines.literal: tomorrow Tuesday is. seven half o'clock! forgotten it not do-you(pl).

notes: ⚠️ This is the trap of the unit — for some learners. Pashto counts the half hour **forward**: اووه نیمې بجې literally means "seven and a half", and it means 7:30 — just like English "half past seven" (or British "half seven"). Languages such as German, Dutch, and Indonesian count it **backward** ("half eight" = 7:30), which is why Budi gets lost. Portuguese, Hungarian, and Persian count forward, like Pashto.

The safest way never to get it wrong: picture the hour that has already passed, then add. If the minute hand has just left the seven, you are at اووه نیمې. If in doubt in front of someone, just say the plain numbers: اووه دېرش.

The word بجې *baje* means "o'clock", and it is used in the plural: درې **بجې** دي. The word ساعت *sā'at* means an hour as a length of time, and also a watch: درې **ساعته** انتظار وکړم (I waited three hours).

The names of the days are borrowed whole from Persian and use numbers: دوشنبه literally "two after Saturday", سه شنبه "three after Saturday", and so on. Once you know that شنبه means Saturday, you can work out five of the other days yourself.

The day off in Afghanistan is **Friday**, not Sunday, and the work week starts on **Saturday**. If you make plans for "the weekend", make sure you are both talking about the same days — this causes misunderstandings far more often than getting the time wrong.
The sentence هېر یې نه کړئ means "don't forget". A prohibition properly uses مه, but the form نه کړئ is also common and sounds a little softer. Commands and prohibitions are covered fully in unit 16.

grammars.title: ⚠️ Telling the time: the half counts FORWARD
body: The question is always the same: څو بجې دي؟ *tso baje dī*, "what time is it?". The answer is a number plus بجې, with the plural verb دي or the past form وې.
For a quarter to the next hour, Pashto uses the Persian borrowing **پونې** *pūne*: پونې څلور means 3:45. You can skip this part for now; saying the plain numbers is always safe.

grammars.title: Seven days and five parts of the day
body: The names of the days are borrowed from Persian and built from numbers, with شنبه (Saturday) as the starting point. In Afghanistan the native Pashto forms څلورشنبه and پنځشنبه are also heard, and they are just as correct as the Persian ones.
The parts of the day matter more than they seem, because Afghans make appointments by part of the day more often than by the clock: سهار (morning), ماسپښین (afternoon), ماښام (dusk).

blocks.text: The time words you'll use most

blocks.title: Afghan time, and what to make allowances for
items: Afghanistan is half an hour off the round hours (UTC+4:30): 12:00 noon in Kabul is 7:30 a.m. in London (GMT) and 12:30 in Pakistan. Afghans think nothing of this half-hour difference.

The official calendar is not the Gregorian one but the Persian solar year, and the new year falls on **نوروز** *Nawroz*, the first day of spring, around March 21. The year 2026 is roughly the year ۱۴۰۵.
Spoken promises are often closed with **انشاءالله** *inshā'allāh* ("God willing"). It is not a way of dodging; it is a fixed part of any sentence about plans, as it is across the Muslim world.

⚠️ Prayer times are used as reference points for appointments more often than the clock: د مازدیګر لمانځه وروسته (after the afternoon prayer) is a very common way to set a time, and more precise than naming a number.

blocks.title: Months, seasons, and a little weather
items: In Kabul the winter is snowy and temperatures drop below zero; Jalalabad is hardly ever cold. The phrases people use: **ژمی سوړ دی** (winter is cold) and **اوړی ګرم دی** (summer is hot).

The month names follow the solar calendar: **وری، غویی، غبرګولی، چنګاښ، زمری، وږی، تله، لړم، لیندۍ، مرغومی، سلواغه، کب**. You don't need to memorize these twelve names now; just know that they exist and that they are not January.
I always get up at six.
The first day of the work week: ____

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: درې بجې دي — اووه نیمې بجې — نهه او پاو — دولس بجې — پنځه نیمې بجې
څو بجې دي؟ — زه تل شپږ بجې پاڅېږم. — سبا سه شنبه ده. — جمعه رخصتي ده. — زه وخت نه لرم.
څو بجې دي؟ — زه تل شپږ بجې پاڅېږم. — جمعه رخصتي ده. — څلور بجې پارک ته ځو. — سبا سه شنبه ده.
wave: Every time you look at a clock today, say the time in Pashto. If the hand is at the half, pause for a second and make sure you name the hour that has PASSED, not the one that is coming.
